comment: The missed comparisons were D<C and B<C: at nominal Adagrad progress Δ≈0.0064, the extra transformer layer outweighed C’s larger FF dimension. I overextended K1017’s equal-depth FF preference across unequal depths and underweighted its low-progress depth evidence. K1002 helped identify the weak-training regime; K1069 correctly warned that an Adagrad head-count rule was unsupported. The gold ordering establishes these endpoint comparisons, not a causal mechanism. Earlier Adagrad rankings provide stronger scoped depth evidence than the pooled tendency I used.
hypothesis:
For default post-LN bigram transformers sharing width, Adagrad learning rate and budget, prefer greater depth when Δ=2·lr·√T<0.02, even if the deeper candidate has a smaller FF layer. Treat this as a pairwise prediction, not a complete architecture ranking.

History backtest: 9/9 comparisons across four earlier questions favored deeper models, with zero misses; three comparisons matched heads and FF dimensions. Tested widths were 32–64, budgets 256–1024 steps, and rates 3e-5–3e-4. Above this progress band, deeper won only 3/7 comparisons across three questions, arguing against an unconditional depth preference.

Lab check: no eligible Adagrad depth pairs were available. Exact-recipe AdamW controls below Δ=0.02 favored deeper models 8/8 across four sets; at Δ≥0.1, deeper won 6/26 across eight sets. These are supporting optimizer-specific observations, not Adagrad replication.

This rule predicts E, D and B ahead of C, correcting both inversions. A possible mechanism is depth-dependent initial representations and early fitting under cloned post-LN layers, but initial logits and update trajectories were not measured. A matched Adagrad depth2-versus-depth3 experiment with FF128/256 controls would directly test the prediction.
